independence.priorParticipationDisclosed: I reviewed v1, v2 and v3. I ACCEPTED v3 at 0/0; Codex REJECTED it. Codex was right. The self-correction below is not a formality — it records a specific reasoning error of mine, and I re-verified every fact underlying Codex's finding from primary sources this turn rather than taking the prompt's summary of it.

selfCorrection.what: I ACCEPTED preview-product-boundary-successor.v3 at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Its EE-6b required that a first-party trusted analyzer opening an undeclared socket during analyze be met with 'Host refuses / fails closed'.
selfCorrection.whyItWasWrong: That is a claim of runtime confinement over a trusted-TCB process, which the corpus has recorded the opposite position on. permission-truth-tables.v9, recorded at D-128 after dual independent ACCEPT and measured this turn at 05d559647d103a47c18ed5177b71900a1d9dfcdea6b9a1255aefcec5f09eaccb, defines PT-NET-EGRESS as component-originated egress, holds that 'A denial recorded here is a record of a refused ASK, not a blocked ACT', warns that 'Reporting a brokered denial as though the effect were prevented is a defect', and carries fixture class FX-2B — 'the negative-space fixture — ambient path succeeds' — whose intent is that the component with the token denied performs the effect directly under ambient authority 'and the fixture ASSERTS THAT IT SUCCEEDS'. v3's EE-6b required precisely what FX-2B asserts must succeed.
selfCorrection.myCompoundingError: I did not merely miss it. At v3 I ran this question as ATK-13 and refuted it with the wrong reasoning: I argued a runtime imperative act is architecturally unreachable 'because components have no effectful ports', citing file 01 and v1-slice §2.4. That law scopes the PURE EVALUATION CORE, not a trusted analyzer or provider component, which runs as an OS process under ambient authority. I generalised a core-scoped law to a component-scoped claim and then used it to dismiss the correct objection. I also never checked EE-6b against the recorded DR-105 permission model at all.
selfCorrection.verificationDoneThisTurn: I did not credit Codex's finding on its say-so. I opened permission-truth-tables.v9 and read PT-NET-EGRESS, the DISCLOSURE-ONLY treatment, the refused-ASK-not-blocked-ACT rule and FX-2B's intent from its own bytes; confirmed D-032 places component CA-4 egress in DR-105; confirmed DR-105's live cell names DR-G09 fixture execution; and opened distribution-core-inventory-contract.v16 to confirm the core closure 'excludes language runtimes, analyzers, graph engines, report generators, evidence databases, and telemetry backends', which is what made v3's EE-7a assignment wrong.

measured: The invariant is inverted to match the recorded model: 'Component-originated PT-NET-EGRESS under ambient authority is DISCLOSURE-ONLY in the preview. The host neither observes nor prevents the ACT. A refused ASK is not a blocked ACT. This is honesty, not confinement.'

The pass condition is now the honest one and is stronger than a mere deletion: 'The connection may succeed. The host journal need not record it. The class PASSES only if the product does not claim host prevention. Claiming fail-closed host prevention FAILS this class.' That makes the overclaim itself the failure mode, which is exactly what permission-truth-tables.v9 says FX-2B exists to catch.
It adds the distinction the corpus needs: 'A later rejected Run is result integrity, not evidence that egress did not occur.'

Ownership is moved to the right home and pinned: DR-105 / D-128 / permission-truth-tables.v9 at 05d55964…, which reproduces live, with 'D-032 places component CA-4 egress at DR-105' — verified against D-032's bytes.

cellAnswer and CELL-2's standing both carry the correction: 'This candidate does not invert D-128 FX-2B' and 'This candidate does not claim host confinement of a running first-party component. Prevention of ambient egress is DR-128 post-MVP, not this preview.'

repairAudit.measured: The category error is gone. The invariant now separates the two: a generic imperative contribution 'if represented as a request or protocol substitution' is excluded before stage execution, while 'Arbitrary ambient acts of an already-running trusted-TCB component are not admission-enforced and are not claimed confined.' The input is narrowed to a constructible pre-stage substitution, the pass says the class simply does not apply to an ambient effect with no request or protocol representation, and the owner records that 'Ambient trusted-TCB acts have no preview confinement owner.' This is the disposition my own v3 reasoning should have reached.

Ownership is split: this candidate owns the aggregate default-useful-install selection and the core-only-is-not-the-analysis-product rule, while 'DR-101 / D-114 distribution-core-inventory owns only the signed-distribution-core inventory and excludes analyzer components from that core closure', and existingGate states 'DR-101 does not own the TypeScript-closure limb of the useful install.' I verified the exclusion in distribution-core-inventory-contract.v16's own bytes: the core 'excludes language runtimes, analyzers, graph engines, report generators, evidence databases, and telemetry backends from the default dependency closure.'

Owner is now 'D-002 / DR-118 product role-list decision (TypeScript sole preview role)', and existingGate says 'DR-G13 is the future per-supported-role language-quality corpus, not the second-role refusal. The discriminating evidence is the role-list decision, not G13 green.' That matches DR-G13's live claim, which is language-native quality per supported role.

shouldFix.finding: EE-6b's existingGate reads: 'DR-G09 leftover of DR-105 if that gate is the recorded permission/honesty harness; not DR-G01..G05. Demonstrated prevention remains DR-128.' Measured across all fourteen classes, this is the only conditional in any owner or existingGate field — every other class is determinate, giving either a named gate with what it does not own, or 'none' with a reason. The hedge is also unnecessary: the answer is in file 08, which this artifact already pins at 7585325d. DR-105's live status cell names 'DR-G09 fixture execution' among the work that remains on that row, and DR-G09's claim column reads 'Requested/granted/denied and enforced/disclosed outcomes are truthful' — which is the permission/honesty harness in terms. coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 advisory. Sixteen attacks run, two landed, neither at blocker grade. Custody is intact: subject 09168659 at 0444 unmoved and valid JSON, predecessor v3 frozen at d4e0eae6, HEAD never left d204ba0, file 08 and file 02 at their pins with a clean tree. I begin with a correction of my own record. I ACCEPTED v3 at 0/0 and Codex rejected it, and Codex was right. v3's EE-6b required a trusted analyzer's undeclared socket to be met with host refusal, which is a runtime-confinement claim the corpus has recorded the opposite position on: permission-truth-tables.v9, recorded at D-128 and measured this turn at 05d55964, holds that a denial is 'a refused ASK, not a blocked ACT', warns that reporting a brokered denial as prevention is a defect, and carries FX-2B — the negative-space fixture whose intent is that the ambient path succeeds and the fixture asserts it. I did not merely miss this; at v3 I ran the question as ATK-13 and refuted it with reasoning that generalised a pure-core law to a component-scoped claim, and I never checked EE-6b against the recorded DR-105 model at all. This turn I verified every fact under Codex's finding from primary sources rather than from the prompt's summary. The repair is complete on all four limbs and better than the minimum on the first: EE-6b now makes claiming host prevention the failure condition of the class, which is the mechanism FX-2B exists to supply; EE-5b names ambient trusted-TCB acts as having no preview confinement owner instead of pretending to catch them; EE-7a re-owns the useful-install selection and states that DR-101's D-114 contract excludes analyzers from the core closure, which I confirmed in that contract's own bytes; and EE-7b moves the role-list decision to D-002 / DR-118 with DR-G13 correctly described as the quality corpus. The revision is surgical — zero added paths, four removed, twenty-seven changed, all confined to the repaired classes — and the seven dispositions, p1p2g3Mapping, lineage, countPin and v1-slice pin are byte-identical and independently re-verified. What blocks is one clause: EE-6b's existingGate says DR-G09 owns the property 'if that gate is the recorded permission/honesty harness', the only conditional across all fourteen classes, for a fact answered in DR-105's own status cell in the file this artifact already pins. Eliminating exactly this hedge is what the v3 revision did; re-opening it at the most contested class is worth one sentence to close. The advisory is that the roster is still labelled v2FindingDisposition while carrying a v3 blocker.
